title: Grade 4 SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — Premium Revision Paper #7

pages.quiz:
SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #7
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. What comes out of a bean seed first when it starts to grow? (1 mark)
   A. A fruit
   B. A new seed
   C. A flower
   D. A root

2. Which of these plants lives for many years? (1 mark)
   A. Sukuma wiki grown for one season
   B. Beans
   C. Mango tree
   D. Maize

3. The touch-me-not plant folds its leaves when touched. This shows that plants can (1 mark)
   A. eat food
   B. respond to changes
   C. lay eggs
   D. move from place to place

4. Which part of a plant makes fruits and seeds? (1 mark)
   A. Flower
   B. Root
   C. Leaf
   D. Stem

5. Which part of the plant takes in water from the soil? (1 mark)
   A. Seed coat
   B. Stem
   C. Flower
   D. Roots

6. A plant with no water for many days will (1 mark)
   A. Make more flowers
   B. Get stronger
   C. Become weak and may die
   D. Grow faster

7. What is the waste passed out by animals called? (1 mark)
   A. Seeds
   B. Milk
   C. Urine and faeces
   D. Food

8. What should you do with a small animal after you observe it? (1 mark)
   A. Return it to where you found it
   B. Squash it
   C. Give it to a friend
   D. Take it home in your pocket

9. Frogs have smooth, wet skin and spend part of their life in water. They are (1 mark)
   A. Birds
   B. Reptiles
   C. Mammals
   D. Amphibians

10. Why is it important to eat slowly? (1 mark)
   A. It stops you growing
   B. It makes you thirsty
   C. It makes food taste of salt
   D. It lets you chew well and helps digestion

11. Which of these describes healthy eating? (1 mark)
   A. Eating only sweets
   B. Eating fruits, vegetables and whole grains
   C. Never drinking water
   D. Eating rotten food

12. Which of these is true about the small intestine? (1 mark)
   A. Digested food passes through its wall into the blood
   B. It stores faeces
   C. It chews food
   D. It swallows food

13. Why is diarrhoea dangerous for young children? (1 mark)
   A. They lose water quickly
   B. They grow more teeth
   C. They sleep too much
   D. They become taller

14. Which of these parts is found before the stomach? (1 mark)
   A. Rectum
   B. Gullet
   C. Small intestine
   D. Large intestine

15. In the dry tissue experiment, why does the tissue stay dry? (1 mark)
   A. The cup is made of plastic
   B. The tissue is warm
   C. Air in the cup keeps the water out
   D. Water cannot touch paper

16. What happens to a gas that is put in a closed jar? (1 mark)
   A. It sits at the top only
   B. It stays at the bottom
   C. It spreads to fill the whole jar
   D. It becomes a solid

17. Which of these is e-waste? (1 mark)
   A. A paper bag
   B. An old phone
   C. A leaf
   D. A banana peel

18. Which of these is non-decomposable? (1 mark)
   A. Plastic bottle
   B. Dry leaves
   C. Fruit peel
   D. Dung

19. Which of these is a source of fresh water? (1 mark)
   A. The sea
   B. A river
   C. A puddle of sea water
   D. A salty lake only

20. What should you do when you see a leaking tap at school? (1 mark)
   A. Tell an adult so it can be fixed
   B. Open it wider
   C. Play with it
   D. Ignore it

21. Which of these is an example of a place where water may be recycled? (1 mark)
   A. A tap
   B. A road
   C. A water treatment plant
   D. A dry shamba

22. Which is a use of gravity? (1 mark)
   A. Lifting up a stone by itself
   B. Making air hot
   C. Making objects float in air
   D. Water flowing downhill

23. Why do people spread ash or sand on a slippery path? (1 mark)
   A. To increase friction
   B. To make it heavy
   C. To reduce friction
   D. To make it hot

24. Which force acts on a ball thrown into the air and brings it back down? (1 mark)
   A. Friction
   B. Sound
   C. Light
   D. Gravity

25. A force can be small or big. A bigger push makes a ball go (1 mark)
   A. Faster and further
   B. Slower
   C. Change colour
   D. Not move

26. What is a force? (1 mark)
   A. A kind of light
   B. A kind of matter
   C. A kind of sound
   D. A push or a pull

27. What effect is shown when a force starts a still football moving? (1 mark)
   A. Changes shape only
   B. Starts motion
   C. Stops motion
   D. Holds it together

28. Which of these is a way of increasing useful friction? (1 mark)
   A. Oiling a floor
   B. Shoes with rough soles
   C. Wearing smooth socks on a wet floor
   D. Polishing a table

29. Which of these is a push? (1 mark)
   A. Drawing water with a rope
   B. Opening a drawer by its handle
   C. Kicking a football
   D. Pulling a cart

30. A pump pushing air into a tyre is an example of (1 mark)
   A. A force
   B. A shadow
   C. A colour
   D. A gas

31. Which of these is a natural source of light? (1 mark)
   A. A torch
   B. A bulb
   C. The sun
   D. A candle

32. Which artificial light uses energy from the sun? (1 mark)
   A. Candle
   B. Firewood
   C. Paraffin lamp
   D. Solar lamp

33. What does a green traffic light tell a driver? (1 mark)
   A. Sleep
   B. Stop
   C. Go
   D. Stop at once

34. Which use of heat makes cloth smooth? (1 mark)
   A. Making shadows
   B. Reading a book
   C. Ironing clothes
   D. Playing music

35. Why is cooking food useful? (1 mark)
   A. It makes food raw
   B. It makes food soft and safer to eat
   C. It makes food dirty
   D. It makes food cold

36. Which of these is a safety rule when cooking? (1 mark)
   A. Leave children alone at the cooker
   B. Touch the hot pot
   C. Turn handles outwards
   D. Turn pot handles inwards

37. Which of these is a safety rule about the sun? (1 mark)
   A. Never look directly at it
   B. Go out at midday without shade
   C. Shine a mirror in eyes
   D. Look at it for a long time

38. At what temperature does water boil? (1 mark)
   A. 50 degrees Celsius
   B. 100 degrees Celsius
   C. 10 degrees Celsius
   D. 0 degrees Celsius

39. Which of these gives out heat when rubbed? (1 mark)
   A. Hands
   B. A stone table
   C. A leaf
   D. A book in a bag

40. Why should kitchen gloves be dry? (1 mark)
   A. Wet cloth is thicker
   B. Dry cloth is heavier
   C. Wet cloth passes heat quickly
   D. Dry cloth is colder

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. Describe the function of each of these parts of a plant: roots, stem, leaves, flowers. (4 marks)

42. Describe an activity to observe the growth of a bean seed. Include what you need, what you do and what you record. (5 marks)

43. Describe how heat is used in cooking and warming in a home. (4 marks)

44. A pupil grows two bean seedlings. One is put in a cupboard and the other in the sunlight. Both are watered. After a week the two look different. Describe what she might see and give a reason. (4 marks)

45. Compare solids, liquids and gases in terms of shape and volume. (4 marks)

46. Describe what happens to food in the stomach. (3 marks)

47. Why is it wrong to say that a tree is not alive because it cannot walk? (3 marks)

48. Describe two properties of a liquid. (3 marks)

49. Explain why plants are called living things. (3 marks)

50. Give three uses of friction in daily life. (3 marks)

51. What is a force? Give one example of a push and one example of a pull. (2 marks)

52. Explain how fibre helps the digestive system. (3 marks)

53. Explain how a school can manage waste at the kitchen, classrooms and playground. (4 marks)

54. Convert 3 litres into millilitres. (2 marks)

55. State two ways of reducing friction. (2 marks)

56. Write two uses of each of these: solids, liquids and gases. (Choose any four uses in all.) (4 marks)

57. Write the function of the rectum and anus. (3 marks)

58. Describe how animals respond to changes around them. Give four examples. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #7 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. D — A root
   The root comes out first and grows down into the soil.

2. C — Mango tree
   Mango trees live for many years, while beans and maize live for one season.

3. B — respond to changes
   Folding when touched is a response to a change in the surroundings.

4. A — Flower
   Flowers make fruits that contain seeds.

5. D — Roots
   Roots take in water and mineral salts.

6. C — Become weak and may die
   Water is needed for life, so a plant without it wilts and may die.

7. C — Urine and faeces
   Animals remove waste such as urine and faeces.

8. A — Return it to where you found it
   Animals should be returned to their home.

9. D — Amphibians
   These features describe amphibians.

10. D — It lets you chew well and helps digestion
   Chewing well breaks food down before swallowing.

11. B — Eating fruits, vegetables and whole grains
   Healthy eating includes fibre and a variety of foods.

12. A — Digested food passes through its wall into the blood
   Absorption takes place there.

13. A — They lose water quickly
   The body loses a lot of water and can become weak.

14. B — Gullet
   Food passes through the gullet before it reaches the stomach.

15. C — Air in the cup keeps the water out
   Air takes up the space inside the cup.

16. C — It spreads to fill the whole jar
   A gas fills any container it is in.

17. B — An old phone
   E-waste means old electrical and electronic items.

18. A — Plastic bottle
   Plastic does not rot easily.

19. B — A river
   Rivers carry fresh water that people can use.

20. A — Tell an adult so it can be fixed
   Reporting leaks helps save water.

21. C — A water treatment plant
   Treatment plants clean used water.

22. D — Water flowing downhill
   Gravity makes water flow downhill.

23. A — To increase friction
   Rough material improves grip.

24. D — Gravity
   Gravity pulls the ball to the ground.

25. A — Faster and further
   A stronger force has a bigger effect.

26. D — A push or a pull
   A force is a push or a pull.

27. B — Starts motion
   A push makes a still object move.

28. B — Shoes with rough soles
   Rough soles grip the ground.

29. C — Kicking a football
   A kick pushes the ball.

30. A — A force
   The pump pushes air by force.

31. C — The sun
   The sun is found in nature.

32. D — Solar lamp
   A solar lamp charges by day.

33. C — Go
   Green means go.

34. C — Ironing clothes
   A hot iron flattens cloth.

35. B — It makes food soft and safer to eat
   Heat kills many germs.

36. D — Turn pot handles inwards
   Handles turned inwards cannot be knocked easily.

37. A — Never look directly at it
   The sun can harm eyes.

38. B — 100 degrees Celsius
   Pure water boils at 100 degrees Celsius.

39. A — Hands
   Rubbing produces heat through friction.

40. C — Wet cloth passes heat quickly
   Wet cloth can burn your hand.

SECTION B
----
41. (4 marks)
   Answer: Roots hold the plant and take in water. The stem supports the plant and carries water and food. Leaves make food. Flowers make fruits and seeds.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct function.

42. (5 marks)
   Answer: You need a tin or container, soil, a bean seed and water. Plant the seed, water a little each day, measure the shoot with a ruler every two days and record heights in a table. Observe roots and leaves.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for materials, 1 mark for planting, 1 mark for watering, 1 mark for measuring, 1 mark for recording.

43. (4 marks)
   Answer: Heat from fire, gas or electricity cooks food making it soft and safer. Heat from fire or clothes keeps the body warm and chicks warm.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of four points.

44. (4 marks)
   Answer: The plant in the cupboard looks weak and pale and the one in the light is green and healthy. Plants need light to make food.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each for describing each plant and 2 marks for the reason.

45. (4 marks)
   Answer: Solid: own shape and fixed volume. Liquid: takes shape of container, fixed volume. Gas: no shape and no fixed volume, fills the container.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each state with correct shape and volume, plus 1 mark for a comparison.

46. (3 marks)
   Answer: The stomach churns the food and mixes it with strong juices. The juices kill many germs and break down the food into a thick soup.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for churns, 1 mark for juices and 1 mark for germs or thick soup.

47. (3 marks)
   Answer: Plants show life in other ways. They grow, reproduce, respond, remove waste and die. Only some animals walk.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for stating plants show signs of life, 1 mark for naming signs, 1 mark for saying walking is not a sign needed for all living things.

48. (3 marks)
   Answer: A liquid has a fixed volume and no shape of its own. It takes the shape of its container and can be poured.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of two properties and 1 mark for the example.

49. (3 marks)
   Answer: They show signs of life. They grow, reproduce, remove waste, respond to changes and die.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for saying they show signs of life and 2 marks for correct signs given.

50. (3 marks)
   Answer: Brakes, shoes gripping the ground, lighting matches, rough tyres, sharpening tools.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.

51. (2 marks)
   Answer: A force is a push or a pull. A push: kicking a ball. A pull: opening a drawer.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the meaning and 1 mark for the two examples.

52. (3 marks)
   Answer: Fibre in fruits, vegetables and whole grains helps food and waste move through the intestines and helps prevent constipation.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for naming fibre foods, 1 mark for movement, 1 mark for constipation.

53. (4 marks)
   Answer: Kitchen: compost pit for food waste and separate bin for plastic. Classroom: bin with lid and paper box. Playground: bins and monitors who pick litter.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each place and 1 mark for a clear system.

54. (2 marks)
   Answer: 3000 ml.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for 3 x 1000 and 1 mark for the answer.

55. (2 marks)
   Answer: Smoothen surfaces, use oil or grease, use rollers, use ball bearings.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.

56. (4 marks)
   Answer: Solids: building, tools, clothes. Liquids: drinking, washing, cooking, fuel. Gases: breathing, cooking gas, inflating tyres.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct use up to 4.

57. (3 marks)
   Answer: The rectum stores faeces for a short time and the anus is the opening through which faeces leave the body.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for rectum, 1 mark for anus, 1 mark for describing waste leaving.

58. (4 marks)
   Answer: A goat lifts its head at noise, a snail pulls into its shell when touched, birds fly away from danger, animals seek shade in hot weather.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the meaning and 1 mark for each of three examples.
